y1: When Judas saw that Jesus was condemned, he regretted it and returned the thirty pieces of silver. The chief priests bought the potter's field with that “blood money”. Meanwhile, the Roman governor Pilate asked, “Are You the King of the Jews?” Jesus said, “You say so,” and remained silent.
y2: Even Pilate's wife said, “Have nothing to do with that righteous man.” But the crowd shouted, “Barabbas!” “Barabbas” means “son of the father”. The sinful “son of the father” was set free, and the sinless “Son of the Father” died.
y3: Pilate washed his hands with water and said, “I am innocent of this man's blood; see to it yourselves.” But responsibility doesn't wash away. The Apostles' Creed still says today, “suffered under Pontius Pilate.”
y5: The soldiers put a scarlet robe on Him, placed a crown of thorns on His head, put a reed in His hand, and mocked Him, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!” What they did was a fake coronation, but it was actually the enthronement of the true King.
y6: Simon of Cyrene was forced to carry the cross. The sign above the cross read, “Jesus, the King of the Jews.” Those passing by, the chief priests, and even the robbers mocked Him, saying, “If You are the Son of God, come down from the cross.” This is the same as Satan's temptation in the wilderness ({Matt. 4:3, 6}).
y7: “He saved others, but He can't save Himself.” The mocking words were true. Because Jesus didn't save Himself, He was able to save others. He could have come down, but He stayed out of love.
y9: From twelve noon until three in the afternoon, the whole land became dark. Jesus cried out with a loud voice: “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?”, that is, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”
y10: This is {Ps. 22:1}. Jesus, bearing sin, experienced separation from the Father. Jesus was forsaken so that we would not be forsaken. Psalm 22 begins with suffering, but ends with victory and praise.
y11: In {Matt. 1:23}, Jesus came as “Immanuel, God is with us”. That Immanuel cries out on the cross, “God has forsaken Me”. Because of this, we are now never forsaken ({Matt. 28:20}).
y13: When Jesus gave up His spirit, the curtain of the temple was torn from top to bottom. It was torn by God, not by man. Now the way to approach God was opened for everyone. The earth shook, the rocks split, and the tombs were opened.
y14: Seeing this, the Roman centurion and the soldiers confessed: “Truly, this was the Son of God.” In the Gospel of Matthew, the first time a person confessed this was at the foot of the cross, and it came from the mouth of a foreign soldier. The rich man Joseph placed Jesus in a new tomb, and the chief priests sealed the tomb and posted a guard.
y15: The disciples fled, but Mary Magdalene and the other women watched from a distance to the end ({Matt. 27:55–56}), and also sat opposite the tomb ({Matt. 27:61}). They will be the first witnesses of the resurrection.
verse: “Now the centurion, and those who were with him watching Jesus, when they saw the earthquake and the things that were done, feared exceedingly, saying, ‘Truly this was the Son of God.’”
prayer: Jesus, even though You were sinless, You were condemned in my place, who am like Barabbas. Even when You were mocked, You did not come down from the cross, and You were forsaken so that I would never be forsaken. I approach God through the way opened by the torn curtain. Truly, You are the Son of God. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: Pilate. He lived in Caesarea and came to Jerusalem during festivals. A stone with his name inscribed on it was found in 1961. He is the only politician mentioned in the Apostles' Creed.
d1: cross. It was a method of execution for slaves and rebels, not applied to Roman citizens. {Deut. 21:23} says, “He who is hanged is accursed of God.” The most cursed instrument of execution became the symbol of the greatest love.
d2: curtain. It was a thick curtain covering the Most Holy Place. Only the high priest could enter there once a year. “He opened a new and living way for us through the curtain, that is, His body” ({Heb. 10:20}).
d3: centurion. Like the centurion in chapter 8, a foreign soldier recognized Jesus. This foreshadows “all nations” in chapter 28. It forms a frame with the worship of the wise men (foreigners) in {Matt. 2:2}.
